readings.title: The Burden of the Word
readings.subtitle: A Rebuke Against Misusing Prophecy
readings.text: [Jeremiah 23:33] “And when these people or the prophet or the priest ask you, saying, ‘What is the message of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?’ then you shall say to them, ‘What message?’ <dq><dn>I</dn> shall forsake you,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [34] <dq>“As for the prophet and the priest and the people who say, ‘The message of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,’ <dn>I</dn> shall punish that man and his house.</dq> [35] <dq>“This is what each one says to his neighbour, and each one to his brother, ‘What has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered?’ and, ‘What has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoken?’</dq> [36] <dq>“But the message of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> you no longer remember! For every man’s message is his own word, for you have changed <dn>את</dn> the Words of the living <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, our <dn>Elohim</dn>!</dq> [37] <dq>“This is what you say to the prophet, ‘What has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered you?’ and, ‘What has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoken?’</dq> [38] <dq>“But since you say, ‘The message of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!’ therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘Because you say <dn>את</dn> this word, “The message of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!” and <dn>I</dn> have sent to you, saying, “Do not say, ‘The message of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!’ ”</dq> [39] <dq>therefore see, <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall utterly forget <dn>את</dn> you and cast <dn>את</dn> you away from <dn>My</dn> presence, along with <dn>את</dn> the city that <dn>I</dn> gave you and your fathers.</dq> [40] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall put an everlasting reproach on you, and an everlasting shame that is not forgotten.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Two Baskets of Figs
readings.subtitle: The Fate of the Exiles and the Remnant
readings.text: [Jeremiah 24:1] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> showed me, and look, there were two baskets of figs set before the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, after Neḇuḵaḏrets-tsar sovereign of Baḇel had exiled <dn>את</dn> Yeḵonyahu son of Yehoyaqim, sovereign of Yehuḏah, and <dn>את</dn> the heads of Yehuḏah with <dn>את</dn> the craftsmen and <dn>את</dn> the smiths, from Yerushalayim, and had brought them to Baḇel. [2] One basket had very good figs, like the figs that are first ripe. And the other basket had very spoilt figs which could not be eaten, they were so spoilt.” [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, “What do you see, Yirmeyahu?” And <dn>I</dn> said, “Figs, the good figs, very good. And the spoilt, very spoilt, which could not be eaten, they are so spoilt.” [4] Again the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [5] <dq>“Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘Like these good figs, so do <dn>I</dn> acknowledge <dn>את</dn> the exiles of Yehuḏah, whom <dn>I</dn> have sent out of this place for their own good, into the land of the Kasdim.</dq> [6] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> eyes on them for good, and shall bring them back to this land. And <dn>I</dn> shall build them and not pull them down, and shall plant them and not pluck them up.</dq> [7] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give them a heart to know <dn>Me</dn>, that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they shall be <dn>My</dn> people and <dn>I</dn> shall be their <dn>Elohim</dn>, for they shall turn back to <dn>Me</dn> with all their heart.</dq> [8] <dq>And as the spoilt figs that could not be eaten because they are so spoilt,’ for thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘so do <dn>I</dn> give up <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏqiyahu, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, <dn>את</dn> his heads, <dn>את</dn> the rest of Yerushalayim who remain in this land, and <dn>את</dn> those who dwell in the land of Mitsrayim.</dq> [9] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall make them a horror to all the reigns of the earth, for evil, to be a reproach and a byword, a mockery and a curse, in all the places to which <dn>I</dn> drive them.</dq> [10] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>את</dn> the sword, <dn>את</dn> the scarcity of food, and <dn>את</dn> the pestilence among them, till they are consumed from the land that <dn>I</dn> gave to them and their fathers.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: A Letter to the Exiles
readings.subtitle: Instructions to Settle in Babylon
readings.text: [Jeremiah 29:1] And these are the words of the letter which Yirmeyah the prophet sent from Yerushalayim to the rest of the elders of the exile, and to the priests, and to the prophets and to all the people whom Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar had exiled from Yerushalayim to Baḇel – [2] after Yeḵonyah the sovereign, and the sovereigness mother, and the eunuchs, and the heads of Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, and the craftsmen, and the smiths had gone into exile from Yerushalayim – [3] by the hand of El‛asah son of Shaphan, and Gemaryah the son of Ḥilqiyah, whom Tsiḏqiyah sovereign of Yehuḏah sent to Baḇel, to Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar the sovereign of Baḇel, saying, [4] <dq>“Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, to all the exiles whom <dn>I</dn> exiled from Yerushalayim to Baḇel,</dq> [5] <dq>Build houses and dwell in them, plant gardens and eat <dn>את</dn> their fruit.</dq> [6] <dq>Take wives and bring forth sons and daughters. And take wives for your sons and give <dn>את</dn> your daughters to husbands, and let them bear sons and daughters, and be increased there, and not diminished.</dq> [7] <dq>And seek <dn>את</dn> the peace of the city where <dn>I</dn> have exiled you, and pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for it, for in its peace you have peace.’</dq>

readings.title: A Promise of Restoration
readings.subtitle: After Seventy Years, a Future and a Hope
readings.text: [Jeremiah 29:8] <dq>“For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘Let not your prophets and your diviners who are in your midst deceive you, neither listen to the dreams which you are dreaming.</dq> [9] <dq>For they are prophesying falsely to you in <dn>My</dn> Name. <dn>I</dn> have not sent them,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [10] <dq>“For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘When seventy years are completed, at Baḇel <dn>I</dn> shall visit you and establish <dn>My</dn> good word toward you, to bring you back to this place.</dq> [11] <dq>For <dn>I</dn> know <dn>את</dn> the plans <dn>I</dn> am planning for you,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘plans of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and an expectancy.</dq> [12] <dq>Then you shall call on <dn>Me</dn>, and shall come and pray to <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> shall listen to you.</dq> [13] <dq>And you shall seek <dn>Me</dn>, and shall find <dn>Me</dn>, when you search for <dn>Me</dn> with all your heart.</dq> [14] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall be found by you,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>’and <dn>I</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> your captivity, and shall gather <dn>את</dn> you from all the nations and from all the places where <dn>I</dn> have driven you, declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring you back to the place from which <dn>I</dn> have exiled you.’</dq>

readings.title: Judgment on False Prophets
readings.subtitle: The Fate of Ahab and Zedekiah
readings.text: [Jeremiah 29:15] “Because you have said, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has raised up prophets for us in Baḇel’ – [16] thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the sovereign who sits on the throne of Daviḏ, concerning all the people who dwell in this city, and concerning your brothers who have not gone out with you into exile, [17] thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am sending on them <dn>את</dn> the sword, <dn>את</dn> the scarcity of food, and <dn>את</dn> the pestilence. And <dn>I</dn> shall make them like spoilt figs, so spoilt as to be uneatable.</dq> [18] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall pursue them with the sword, with scarcity of food, and with pestilence. And <dn>I</dn> shall make them a horror among all the reigns of the earth, to be a curse, and an astonishment, and a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations where <dn>I</dn> have driven them.</dq> [19] <dq>For they did not heed <dn>My</dn> words,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘which <dn>I</dn> sent to them by <dn>My</dn> servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them, yet you did not listen,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [20] “You, therefore, hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all you exiles whom <dn>I</dn> have sent from Yerushalayim to Baḇel. [21] <dq>“Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, concerning Aḥaḇ son of Qolayah, and Tsiḏqiyahu son of Ma‛asěyah, who are prophesying falsely to you in <dn>My</dn> Name, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am giving them into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel, and he shall strike them before your eyes.</dq> [22] <dq>And because of them all the exiles of Yehuḏah who are in Baḇel shall use a curse, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> make you like Tsiḏqiyahu and Aḥaḇ, whom the sovereign of Baḇel roasted in the fire,”</dq> [23] <dq>because they have done wickedness in Yisra’ěl, and committed adultery with their neighbours’ wives, and have spoken a word in <dn>My</dn> Name falsely which <dn>I</dn> have not commanded them. And <dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn> who knows, and a witness,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Letter of Shemaiah
readings.subtitle: A False Prophet Rebuked
readings.text: [Jeremiah 29:24] “And speak to Shemayahu the Neḥelamite, saying, [25] <dq>“Thus speaks <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘Because you have sent letters in your name to all the people who are at Yerushalayim, to Tsephanyah son of Ma‛asěyah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,</dq> [26] <dq>“<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made you priest instead of Yehoyaḏa the priest, so that there are overseers in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> over everyone who is mad and makes himself a prophet, that you should put him in the stocks and in the iron collar.</dq> [27] <dq>“So why have you not reproved Yirmeyahu of Anathoth who makes himself a prophet to you?</dq> [28] <dq>“For he has sent to us in Baḇel, saying, ‘This captivity is long – build houses and dwell in them, and plant gardens and eat their fruit.’ ” ’ ”</dq> [29] And Tsephanyah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Yirmeyahu the prophet. [30] Then the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu, saying, [31] “Send to all those in exile, saying, <dq>‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning Shemayah the Neḥelamite, “Because Shemayah has prophesied to you, and <dn>I</dn> have not sent him, and he has made you to trust on falsehood,”</dq> [32] <dq>therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing punishment upon Shemayah the Neḥelamite and his seed: he shall have no one to dwell among this people, nor is he to see the good that <dn>I</dn> am about to do for <dn>My</dn> people,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“because he has spoken apostasy against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Book of Consolation
readings.subtitle: The Time of Jacob's Trouble and Salvation
readings.text: [Jeremiah 30:1] The word that came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [2] <dq>“Thus spoke <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘Write in a book for yourself <dn>את</dn> all the words that <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you.</dq> [3] <dq>For look, the days are coming,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘when <dn>I</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl and Yehuḏah,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>’and <dn>I</dn> shall bring them back to the land that <dn>I</dn> gave to their fathers, and let them possess it.’ ”</dq> [4] And these are the words <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke concerning Yisra’ěl and Yehuḏah. [5] <dq>“For this is what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, ‘We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.</dq> [6] <dq>Ask now, and see if a man is giving birth. Why do <dn>I</dn> see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labour, and all faces turned pale?</dq> [7] <dq>Oh! For great is that day, there is none like it. And it is the time of Ya‛aqoḇ’s distress, but he shall be saved out of it.</dq> [8] <dq>And it shall be in that day,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘that <dn>I</dn> break his yoke from your neck, and tear off your bonds, and foreigners no more enslave them.</dq> [9] <dq>And they shall serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn> and <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ their sovereign, whom <dn>I</dn> raise up for them.</dq> [10] <dq>And you, do not fear, O Ya‛aqoḇ <dn>My</dn> servant,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘nor be discouraged, O Yisra’ěl. For look, <dn>I</dn> am saving you from afar, and <dn>את</dn> your seed from the land of their captivity. And Ya‛aqoḇ shall return, and have rest and be at ease, with no one to trouble him.</dq> [11] <dq>For <dn>I</dn> am with you,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘to save you. Though <dn>I</dn> make a complete end of all nations where <dn>I</dn> have scattered you, yet <dn>I</dn> do not make a complete end of you. But <dn>I</dn> shall reprove you in judgment, and by no means leave you unpunished.’</dq>

readings.title: An Incurable Wound Healed
readings.subtitle: Restoration for the Outcast Zion
readings.text: [Jeremiah 30:12] <dq>“For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘Your breach is incurable, your wound is grievous.</dq> [13] <dq>No one pleads your cause, to bind up. There are no healing medicines for you.</dq> [14] <dq>All those loving you have forgotten you, they do not seek you. For <dn>I</dn> struck you as an enemy strikes, with cruel chastisement, because your crookedness is great, your sins have increased.</dq> [15] <dq>Why do you cry about your breach? Your pain is incurable. Because of your many crookednesses, because your sins have increased, <dn>I</dn> have done this to you.</dq> [16] <dq>However, all those who devour you shall be devoured. And all your adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity. And those who exploit you shall be exploited, and all who prey upon you <dn>I</dn> shall make a prey.</dq> [17] <dq>For <dn>I</dn> restore health to you and heal you of your wounds,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘for they have called you an outcast saying, “This is Tsiyon, no one is seeking her.” ’</dq>

readings.title: The Restoration of Jacob's Tents
readings.subtitle: A Prince from Among Them
readings.text: [Jeremiah 30:18] <dq>“Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of Ya‛aqoḇ’s tents, and have compassion on his dwelling places. And the city shall be built upon its own mound, and the palace stand on its right place.</dq> [19] <dq>And out of them shall arise thanksgiving and the voice of those who are laughing. And <dn>I</dn> shall increase them, and they shall not diminish. And <dn>I</dn> shall esteem them, and they shall not be small.</dq> [20] <dq>And his children shall be as before, and his congregation shall be established before <dn>Me</dn>. And <dn>I</dn> shall punish all who oppress them.</dq> [21] <dq>And his Prince shall be from him, and his Ruler shall come from among him. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring him near, and he shall approach <dn>Me</dn>, for who is this who pledged his heart to approach <dn>Me</dn>?’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [22] <dq>And you shall be <dn>My</dn> people, and <dn>I</dn> shall be your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq> [23] See, the storm of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall go forth in a rage, a whirling storm! It bursts upon the head of the wrong. [24] The burning displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall not turn back until <dn>He</dn> has done and established <dn>את</dn> the purposes of <dn>His</dn> heart. In the latter days you shall understand it.

readings.title: An Everlasting Love
readings.subtitle: Israel to be Rebuilt and Rejoice
readings.text: [Jeremiah 31:1] <dq>“At that time,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall be the <dn>Elohim</dn> of all the clans of Yisra’ěl, and they shall be <dn>My</dn> people.”</dq> [2] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “A people escaped from the sword found favour in the wilderness, Yisra’ěl, when it went to find rest.” [3] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to me from afar, saying, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have loved you with an everlasting love, therefore <dn>I</dn> shall draw you with loving-commitment.</dq> [4] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am going to build you again. And you shall be rebuilt, O maiden of Yisra’ěl! Again you shall take up your tambourines, and go forth in the dances of those who rejoice.</dq> [5] <dq>“Again you shall plant vines on the mountains of Shomeron. The planters shall plant and treat them as common.</dq> [6] <dq>“For there shall be a day when the watchmen cry on Mount Ephrayim, ‘Arise, and let us go up to Tsiyon, to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Joyful Return
readings.subtitle: Gathering the Remnant from the Ends of the Earth
readings.text: [Jeremiah 31:7] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Sing with gladness for Ya‛aqoḇ, and shout among the chief of the nations. Cry out, give praise, and say, ‘O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, save <dn>את</dn> Your people, <dn>את</dn> the remnant of Yisra’ěl!’</dq> [8] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing them from the land of the north, and shall gather them from the ends of the earth, among them the blind and the lame, those with child and those in labour, together – a great assembly returning here.</dq> [9] <dq>“With weeping they shall come, and with their prayers <dn>I</dn> bring them. <dn>I</dn> shall make them walk by rivers of waters, in a straight way in which they do not stumble. For <dn>I</dn> shall be a Father to Yisra’ěl, and Ephrayim – he is <dn>My</dn> first-born.</dq> [10] “Hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, O nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, <dq>‘<dn>He</dn> who scattered Yisra’ěl gathers him, and shall guard him as a shepherd his flock.’</dq> [11] <dq>“For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall ransom <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ, and redeem him from the hand of one stronger than he.</dq> [12] <dq>“And they shall come in and shall sing on the height of Tsiyon, and stream to the goodness of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for grain and for new wine and for oil, and for the young of the flock and the herd. And their being shall be like a well-watered garden, and never languish again.</dq> [13] <dq>“Then shall a maiden rejoice in a dance, and young men and old, together. And <dn>I</dn> shall turn their mourning to joy, and shall comfort them, and shall make them rejoice from their sorrow,</dq> [14] <dq>and shall fill the being of the priests with fatness. And <dn>My</dn> people shall be satisfied with <dn>My</dn> goodness,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
